title: Quality-Cost Synthesis & Correlation Playbook
author: Priya Nambiar
content:
Overview

Purpose: Provide a single reference that ties together LLM quality signals (regressions, hallucination proxies, eval failures) with unit-cost signals (token spend, GPU-seconds, quantization fallbacks) so operators and product owners can triage cost vs. quality tradeoffs quickly. This playbook defines dashboards, PromQL/SQL examples, alert rules, investigation steps, and a lightweight escalation matrix.

When to use this doc:
- New alert: cost is rising but latency is stable
- Quality regression: eval failure trend correlates with a recent runtime change or model variant swap
- Planning: onboarding a heavy tenant and validating cost/quality projections

Key concepts and definitions
- Token-unit cost: token spend normalized by model variant and sequence length; baseline metric is tokens_per_1k_requests.
- Quality q-score: weighted composite (per-customer) of eval-set pass rate, automated hallucination proxy, and human feedback rate. Scaled 0..100.
- Cost drift event: sustained >15% increase in token-unit cost for 24h over baseline (baseline is 7d rolling median).
- Quality regression: drop in q-score >=5 points vs. 7d rolling median for an owner-specified prompt-set.

Dashboards (required panels)
1) Cost synthesis overview (single pane)
   - Panels:
     * Token spend (1h/6h/24h) by model_variant, region, tenant
     * GPU-hrs consumed by tenant (24h / 7d)
     * Effective tokens_per_1k_requests (rolling 6h) with trendline
     * Cost-per-successful-inference (token_cost / successful_requests)

2) Quality synthesis overview (single pane)
   - Panels:
     * q-score (tenant, model_variant) — 1h/6h/24h
     * Eval failure rate by prompt-set and rollout cohort
     * Hallucination-proxy rate (defined below)
     * Human-reported correctness (sampled)

3) Correlation canvas (heatmap)
   - Heatmap rows: tenants / model_variants; columns: time buckets (1h)
   - Cell color: Pearson correlation coefficient between token-cost-per-request and q-score over a sliding 24h window.

4) Root-cause drill panels (hidden by default; auto-expand on alert)
   - KV cache hit ratio by tenant and prefix
   - Batch size distribution histogram (requests per batch)
   - Model compilation path / kernel selection frequency (labels: kernel=vNN)
   - Recent rollouts and config-change audit log (last 48h)

Example queries and snippets
- PromQL (token spend per model variant, 1h rate):

  rate(redwood_tokens_consumed_total{job="runtime",environment!="staging"}[1h]) by (model_variant)

- SQL (q-score by tenant, last 24h):

  SELECT tenant_id, avg(q_score) AS q_score_24h
  FROM inference_quality_events
  WHERE ts >= now() - INTERVAL '24 hours'
  GROUP BY tenant_id;

- Hallucination proxy (heuristic): fraction of responses with >N factuality-mismatch signals (N=2) across 1k sampled responses. Implementation detail: run lightweight fact-checker on sampled outputs and count mismatches.

Alerting rules (sensible defaults)
- High-cost anomaly (severity: P2)
  * Trigger: cost drift event (token-unit cost + GPU-hrs) for a tenant or model_variant for 24h AND no corresponding increase in q-score (>+2).
  * PromQL example (tokens_per_1k burst):

    increase(redwood_token_cost_per_1k{tenant="$tenant"}[24h]) / (24) > 1.15 * avg_over_time(redwood_token_cost_per_1k{tenant="$tenant"}[7d])

  * Primary recipient: platform-cost-alerts (PagerDuty), secondary: tenant SRE/AE channel.

- Quality drop correlated with cheaper model (severity: P1)
  * Trigger: q-score drop >=5 pts for a tenant AND deployment history shows model_variant change OR quantization flag toggled in last 6h.
  * Notify: model-onboarding and product-quality teams, Ops on-call.

- Cost-quality divergence (severity: P2)
  * Trigger: correlation coefficient between cost and quality in the last 24h < -0.5 AND absolute cost upward shift >15%.
  * Action: open automated incident in incident-tracker with correlation heatmap attached.

Ownership and runbook flow
- Owners:
  * Dashboards & alerts: Platform Observability (eng-platform) — primary: @oncall-platform-observability
  * Cost analytics: Finance Ops — primary: @finops
  * Quality tooling and evals: Applied ML & Evals — primary: @applied-ml

- Runbook (triage sequence)
  1. Acknowledge alert and check correlation canvas. Note tenant, model_variant, and time window.
  2. Open per-tenant root-cause drill panels (KV cache / batch size / kernels).
  3. Check recent deploys and config changes: run

     curl -s "https://audit.internal/api/changes?after=48h&tenant=$TENANT" | jq .

  4. If model_variant changed or quant flag toggled in last 6h: roll back to previous variant (if safe) or trigger canary re-evaluation.
  5. If no deployment changes, look at traffic characteristics: increased average seq_len or increased external latency causing larger batches. If average_seq_len increased >20% in 6h, notify product owner for traffic pattern analysis.
  6. If KV cache hit ratio < 60% and cost spike present: prioritize cache warmup / prefix prefetch for affected tenants.
  7. If hallucination-proxy increased and cost decreased (cheaper model): label as "quality-regression-due-to-variant" and engage Applied ML for evaluation.
  8. Document findings in the incident ticket and attach correlation heatmap.

Escalation matrix
- P1 (severity high quality regression): PagerDuty to Applied ML (30m SLA), notify Eng VPs if unresolved after 2 hours.
- P2 (cost divergence): Platform Observability PD (1 hour SLA), FinOps loop-in after 4 hours if cost continues to increase.
- P3 (informational): Slack alert to dashboards channel; weekly digest for owners.

Dashboard templates and panel config examples
- Minimal Grafana panel JSON (tokens_per_1k requests, trendline):

  {
    "type": "timeseries",
    "title": "Tokens per 1k requests — {{tenant}}",
    "targets": [
      {"expr": "rate(redwood_tokens_consumed_total{tenant=\"$tenant\"}[1h]) / (sum(rate(redwood_requests_total{tenant=\"$tenant\"}[1h])) by (tenant) * 1000)", "format": "time_series"}
    ]
  }

- Heatmap generation note: use 24h sliding windows and compute Pearson R in the backend job (not in dashboard) to keep panels responsive. Backend job should write a metric redwood_cost_quality_corr{tenant,model_variant,window_start} with value in [-1,1].

Operational guidelines for experiments and rollouts
- Canary checks: when adding a cheaper model_variant to a rollout, ensure automated canary has the following gates:
  1) q-score delta within -1.5 pts for primary prompt-sets (1h window)
  2) Token-unit cost improvement >= 10% for expected traffic mix
  3) No increase in hallucination-proxy above 0.5 percentage points

- Experiment metrics to capture in every rollout: token_cost_per_1k, q_score, kv_cache_hit_ratio, avg_batch_size, p90_latency. Keep these for 90 days.

Post-incident and retrospective guidance
- If a cross-cutting incident (cost-quality divergence) occurs, the owning teams must produce a 2-week retro that includes:
  * Timeline and annotated correlation heatmap
  * Root cause hypothesis and evidence (queries, diffs of rollout configs)
  * Cost impact (dollars) and quality impact (users affected, q-score delta)
  * Action plan with owners and completion dates

Appendix: Implementation checklist (minimum viable rollout)
- [ ] Backend job computing cost-quality Pearson R every hour and exporting as metric
- [ ] Grafana dashboard with panels described above and templating for tenant/model_variant
- [ ] Alert rules added to Alertmanager with PagerDuty integration and runbook links
- [ ] Sample SQL queries and lightweight fact-checker pipeline for hallucination proxy
- [ ] 7d baseline computation job for token-unit cost and q-score
